title: Pipeline Stage-Level Architecture

scope.purpose: Describe the reusable structural responsibilities and relationships of a Stage Template and its concrete instances, without defining workflow-specific processing semantics or implementation details.
scope.appliesTo: Any concrete Stage Instance conforming to the reusable Stage contract; it is not limited to the thirteen Generator processing stages.

stage.definition: A bounded orchestration component that exposes a Stage-level interface to its consuming workflow and internally coordinates the Step Instances required by that Stage.
responsibilities: Expose the Stage contract to its consuming workflow.
Own the composition of Step Instances belonging to the Stage.
Coordinate invocation of its Steps through their Stage-facing callable contracts.

Define the Stage-specific internal execution structure, dependencies, transition conditions, and flow-decision semantics; execution of the corresponding native workflow graph may be delegated to the selected external Workflow Framework under those GPWCF-defined semantics.
Manage the Stage-specific flow semantics and determine the final Stage-specific Flow Result from the execution facts returned by the execution mechanism.
Publish the Stage outputs and execution status required by the consuming workflow.
Define and register Stage-owned error type definitions through the StageErrorTypeDefinitionRegistry Instance assigned to the Stage by the consuming workflow where the common Error Model requires it.
Create StageError occurrences for errors arising within Stage-owned responsibilities, using definitions registered in its assigned Registry.
doesNotOwn: The semantic ownership of artifacts assigned to another Stage by the consuming workflow's contracts.
The internal processing implementation or component topology of an individual Step.
The implementation details of Step-specific SPUs, validators, error models, error-handling units, or observation units.

stageFacade.role: Provide the Stage-level boundary and interface through which the Pipeline invokes and receives results from the Stage.
responsibilities: Present the Stage execution contract without exposing internal Step composition.
Accept the Stage-level inputs defined by the concrete Stage specialization.
Return the Stage-level outputs and status defined by the concrete Stage specialization.
stageFacade.implementationForm: The facade is an architectural role. Whether it is implemented as a distinct class or another explicit interface realization is not prescribed here.

stepComposition.role: Own the semantic composition and flow rules of the Step Instances belonging to the Stage; coordinate their contract-level participation and result collection while allowing an external Workflow Framework to execute the corresponding native Parent Workflow graph.
responsibilities: Maintain the Stage-specific set of Step Instances.
Coordinate their invocation through their public Stage-facing Step contracts.
Respect the Stage-specific dependencies and execution constraints.

Own the meaning, conditions, and permitted outcomes of the Stage-specific flow and transitions between Steps. Where an external Workflow Framework executes the Stage as a native Parent Workflow, its runtime may evaluate and enact those GPWCF-defined conditions and transitions without acquiring semantic ownership or requiring a second GPWCF scheduler.
Determine when a Step Instance is to be created or acquired, reused, and released as required by the Stage's execution and lifecycle needs.
Coordinate Step Instance lifecycle decisions without prescribing or owning the concrete lifecycle mechanism used by an individual Step.
Collect and retain the StepExecutionResult produced by each Step invocation that returns a result.
Record invocation exceptions independently from StepExecutionResult when a Step invocation terminates by throwing and does not return a result.
Determine the Stage-specific response to an invocation exception; no universal exception-handling action or policy is imposed at this architectural level.
Compose the final Flow Result from the execution information and flow context relevant to the Stage.
Consume StageError occurrences and other Stage execution information relevant to flow coordination.
Determine the Stage-specific response to StageError occurrences and represent them in the Flow Result or another Stage-owned result contract as defined by that Stage.
A Stage Composition may create a StageError occurrence when an error arises within its own responsibility; it is not the exclusive creator of StageError occurrences.
Choose whether the current Stage-level use of a Step ends with retention for reuse or terminal retirement, according to Stage-specific lifecycle needs.
Request the selected disposition through the Step public lifecycle boundary and consume its confirmed, failed, or indeterminate outcome.
Do not treat request submission as completion or make an unresolved Step eligible for reuse or destruction.
Retain or explicitly transfer recovery responsibility/access for a Step whose terminal retirement remains unresolved.
stepComposition.implementationForm: The composition is an architectural responsibility. A separate Composite class is not mandated by this document.

flowResult.role: Represent the result of the Stage's internal Step-execution flow, independently of the result of any individual Step invocation.
responsibilities: Represent the outcome of the Stage-specific flow after the flow has reached its Stage-defined completion point.
Allow the Stage-specific Flow Result to retain or aggregate StepExecutionResult values returned by Step invocations during the flow.
Allow the Stage-specific Flow Result to record Step invocation exceptions independently from returned StepExecutionResult values.
Represent, as appropriate to the Stage, the flow decisions and transitions and the execution context at which the flow concluded.
Retain or represent StageError occurrences when required by the owning Stage's Flow Result design.
constraints: Flow Result is an independent result contract; it is neither a StepExecutionResult nor an extension or specialization of StepExecutionResult.
A StepExecutionResult describes one Step invocation that returned an execution result; Flow Result describes the Stage's overall Step-execution flow.
An invocation exception that prevents a Step from returning StepExecutionResult must not be represented as a StepExecutionResult.
The occurrence or recording of an invocation exception does not, by itself, prescribe the final Flow Result or determine that the flow must fail.

The detailed Flow Result structure, the representation of retained execution results and exceptions, and the rules for composing the result are Stage-specific; no uniform schema or composition policy is mandated here.

A StageError occurrence is created by the Stage-owned component whose responsibility produces the error; Stage Composition consumes the resulting error information and determines the Stage-specific flow response.
The Stage defines how StageError occurrences are represented in its Flow Result or another Stage-owned result contract; no universal StageError-to-FlowResult schema is imposed.
A thrown exception is not automatically converted into a StageError occurrence.

externalWorkflowIntegration.purpose: Define how a Stage's GPWCF-owned Stage/Step composition semantics are realized as a native Stage Parent Workflow by an external Workflow Framework while preserving the Stage public boundary and Stage-specific result semantics.
semanticAuthority: The concrete Stage specialization and its Stage Composition own the selected Step membership, functional responsibilities, Step-facing invocation contracts, permitted dependencies, transition conditions, flow-decision meanings, exception-response semantics, and Stage Flow Result assembly rules.
This authority defines the Stage's intended behavior and constraints; it does not require GPWCF to schedule or dispatch the native workflow graph.
nativeExecutionRealization: Where an external Workflow Framework is selected, the Stage may be realized as a native Parent Workflow whose child Step executions are native nested workflows/subworkflows.

The external runtime executes the native Stage graph, including scheduling/dispatch and evaluation/enactment of GPWCF-defined Stage transition conditions, subject to the Stage specialization's declared semantics.
Each Step must be invoked through its public Stage-facing Step contract. The native realization must not bypass a Step boundary by directly invoking its internal SPUs or Supporting Units.

The Stage facade remains the Pipeline-facing boundary. The Pipeline/root integration invokes the Stage contract and consumes the Stage-defined outputs, execution status, and Flow Result as applicable; it does not own Stage-internal topology.
The integration must not create a second GPWCF scheduler, universal graph executor, or alternate source of Stage flow semantics.
resultAndFailurePreservation: Each Step invocation's returned StepExecutionResult remains distinct from a thrown invocation exception and remains attributable to its originating Step invocation.
The native runtime's workflow/task status is execution evidence only; it does not replace StepExecutionResult, Stage Flow Result, Stage outputs, or Stage-defined execution status.

The Stage Flow Result remains the Stage-owned representation of the Stage's Step-execution flow, including the Stage-defined treatment of returned Step results, invocation exceptions, transitions, and StageError occurrences.
Stage identity, Step identity, parent/child invocation correlation, context, and result provenance remain traceable across native workflow boundaries.
functionalBinding: The Stage facade and each Step public callable contract are bound to the corresponding native workflow invocation boundary without exposing internal implementation details.

The exact native relationship mechanism is selected according to its semantics (for example, workflow composition, parent-child invocation, containment, or another native construct); no Association construct is mandatory merely because the Pipeline root coordinates multiple Stages.
Any specialized Association semantics remain governed by their existing contracts and are not generalized by this Stage-level integration clause.
nonMandates: No universal Pipeline or Stage runtime, scheduler, workflow graph representation, adapter, plugin manager, registry, or generic result model is introduced.
No particular external Workflow Framework, native workflow type, or relationship mechanism is mandated.
External execution authority does not transfer ownership of Stage/Step domain semantics or Stage Flow Result assembly to the external runtime.

constraints: A Stage must not bypass a Step's Stage-facing execution contract by invoking its internal SPUs or supporting units directly.
A Stage may contain a Stage-specific number and arrangement of Step Instances; uniform Step counts or identical internal workflows across Stages are not required.
The internal execution order, branching, repetition, concurrency, and dependency rules are defined by the owning Stage specialization, not inferred from the Stage-level structure.
Stage-level outputs must conform to the authoritative contracts defined by the consuming workflow.
The Stage architecture must preserve the distinction between Stage orchestration, Step orchestration, and SPU processing responsibilities.
StepExecutionResult and Flow Result are distinct contracts with distinct scopes; neither is defined as an extension or specialization of the other.
Each returned StepExecutionResult remains attributable to the Step invocation that produced it and available to Stage Composition for flow coordination.
Invocation exceptions are recorded separately from returned StepExecutionResult values, and recording an exception does not impose a universal flow-control response.

Stage Composition owns lifecycle decisions about when a Step Instance is created or acquired, reused, and released when lifecycle management is required; the concrete lifecycle mechanism remains associated with the individual Step.
No universal Step lifecycle policy, exception-handling action, Flow Result schema, or Flow Result composition policy is imposed across Stages.
Flow Result is distinct from the Stage outputs and Stage execution status exposed through the Stage facade; their exact relationship is defined by the owning Stage contract.
Ending Stage-level use of a Step is distinct from terminal retirement; Stage Composition explicitly selects the intended disposition.
Stage Composition requests retention/reuse or terminal retirement only through the public Step boundary and never manages internal SPU/supporting-unit lifecycles.
A Step is terminally retired only after its public contract reports confirmed completion; request acceptance, timeout, reference loss, or destructor execution is insufficient.
Failed/indeterminate lifecycle outcomes remain Stage-owned coordination facts requiring a Stage-specific response; no universal continue, abort, or retry policy is imposed.
Stage Composition does not discard the only access path or recovery responsibility while retirement remains unresolved.

references.relationship: result contract for an individual Step invocation

openDesignDetails: The exact Stage-level input and output type contracts are defined per concrete Stage.
The exact Stage facade and composition implementation types remain an implementation-level decision.
Stage-specific execution topology and flow-control decisions are defined in each consuming workflow's Stage specialization.

The detailed Flow Result structure and representation or aggregation of its StepExecutionResult records, invocation exceptions, flow decisions, transitions, and terminal execution context are defined per Stage.
The exact relationship between a Stage-specific Flow Result and the Stage outputs and execution status exposed to the consuming workflow is defined by the owning Stage contract.

Each concrete Stage defines when a Step is retained for reuse versus terminally retired and its response to confirmed, failed, or indeterminate outcomes; Step defines the public boundary and Step Composition defines internal settlement.

stageErrorResponsibilities.definitionOwnership: The concrete Stage owns the specialized StageErrorTypeDefinition types and definitions for its Stage-level error domain.
stageErrorResponsibilities.registration: The Stage registers its StageErrorTypeDefinition instances through the StageErrorTypeDefinitionRegistry Instance assigned to it by the Pipeline. The Pipeline retains exclusive ownership of that Registry Instance.
stageErrorResponsibilities.occurrenceCreation: A Stage-owned component creates a StageError[TErrorOccurrenceContext] occurrence when an error arises within that component's Stage-owned responsibility. Stage Composition may create occurrences for errors arising within its own responsibility but is not the exclusive occurrence producer.
stageErrorResponsibilities.flowConsumption: Stage Composition consumes StageError information as relevant to Stage flow coordination and determines the Stage-specific response and representation.
stageErrorResponsibilities.exceptionSeparation: Thrown exceptions remain distinct from StageError occurrences unless an explicit Stage-owned contract defines a conversion; no automatic conversion is implied.
